audience.text: Python developers and data scientists who need to embed TeX processing in applications without installing external TeX engines or fonts.

capabilities.text: The library parses real TeX/LaTeX source through its own from-scratch interpreter, driving tokenizer, macro expander, and mode-machine dispatch.
capabilities.title: Parse and interpret TeX source

capabilities.text: Output devices PdfDevice, DviDevice, and SvgDevice convert finished pages to their respective formats, supporting both in-memory and file output.
capabilities.title: Produce PDF, DVI, and SVG output

capabilities.text: Font metrics and glyph outlines are resolved from bundled Computer Modern .tfm/.pfb data, with SVG output embedding glyph outlines as <path> elements.
capabilities.title: Embed bundled Computer Modern fonts

capabilities.text: The create_input_source factory returns FileInputSource or StringInputSource from Path, str, or bytes inputs.
capabilities.title: Support input from strings, files, and bytes

capabilities.text: The optional mcp extra installs the mcp package and exposes compile_tex, tex_to_pdf, tex_to_svg, and tex_version functions.
capabilities.title: Provide MCP server for external integration

capabilities.text: TeXJob.messages returns collected diagnostics, and the package supports Python logging for engine output via the aspose_tex logger.
capabilities.title: Support job diagnostics and logging

limitations.text: LaTeX and e-TeX/pdTeX extensions are not implemented; commands like documentclass, numexpr, and pdfoutput raise EngineError.
Named file-stream I/O (openin, openout, closein, closeout, read, write to streams 0–15) raises NotImplementedError; only write 16, write -1, message, and errmessage are implemented.
Automatic hyphenation requires the plain format; with load_format=False no patterns are loaded, and other languages need custom format files.
The package is a Pre-Alpha release; core engine and public API are under active development and interfaces may change between releases.
The default format is plain TeX; LaTeX support is not implemented and raises errors for LaTeX-specific commands.
The package registers a logging.NullHandler by default; applications must explicitly configure logging to see engine output.

problems_solved.text: Enables TeX processing in Python environments without external dependencies like MiKTeX or TeX Live.
Provides bundled Computer Modern fonts and format data, removing the need to install or locate system fonts.
Supports both in-memory and file-based output for PDF, DVI, and SVG formats through a unified API.

product_summary.text: Aspose.TeX FOSS for Python is a free, open-source, pure-Python library for processing TeX/LaTeX source, producing PDF, DVI, and SVG output without requiring an external TeX installation.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported TeX primitives and control sequences beyond those shown in examples is not fully documented.
The behavior of extra_format_paths when multiple format files exist is not detailed beyond search order.
Whether the mcp server supports concurrent requests or has performance characteristics is not specified.
The exact version of Computer Modern fonts bundled and their licensing details beyond the separate LICENSE-FONTS file are not provided.
The scope of the 'Pre-Alpha' status beyond API instability (e.g., feature completeness, known bugs) is not detailed.
How the library handles out-of-memory or resource exhaustion during long-running jobs is not described.
The exact behavior of get_all_pages() when called before run() or on a single-page job is not specified.
Whether the library supports non-ASCII input encodings beyond UTF-8 is not stated.

workflows.name: Create and run a TeX job in memory
workflows.text: Create an input source from a string, instantiate a device (e.g., PdfDevice), configure options, run the job, and retrieve output bytes.

workflows.name: Write output directly to a file
workflows.text: Pass a Path to a device constructor, run the job, and let the library write the output file without returning bytes.

workflows.name: Process multi-page SVG output
workflows.text: Run a job with SvgDevice, then call get_all_pages() to retrieve a list of SVG byte strings, one per page.

workflows.name: Configure job options
workflows.text: Set job_name, magnification, and extra_format_paths via TeXOptions to customize job behavior.

workflows.name: Collect diagnostics and logging
workflows.text: Access TeXJob.messages after running to retrieve plain-text diagnostic entries, and configure Python logging for engine output.
